# Kerala ranked 19th in NITI Aayog’s India Electric Mobility Index

## With an overall score of 36 out of a possible 100, Kerala has been adjudged ‘Aspirant’ State in the rankings which assess performance on three core themes: progress of transport electrification, readiness of charging infrastructure, and status of research and innovation in electric vehicles

Updated  - August 07, 2025 04:19 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM

Tiki Rajwi

SEE ALL
Remove

Kerala has been ranked 19th in the first India Electric Mobility Index 2024 (IEMI) published by the NITI Aayog for tracking the progress of electric mobility made by States and Union Territories.

With an overall score of 36 out of a possible 100, Kerala has been adjudged ‘Aspirant’ State in the rankings which assess performance on three core themes: progress of transport electrification, readiness of charging infrastructure, and status of research and innovation in electric vehicles.

Kerala has been ranked 21st in transport electrification, 11th in EV research and innovation, and 24th in the readiness of charging infrastructure. Kerala shares the 19th position overall with Jharkhand.

No State has scored 100 to claim ‘Achiever’ status. Delhi (score 77), Maharashtra (68), and Chandigarh (65) have been respectively ranked one, two, and three and listed as the only three ‘Front-runners’ on the list. They are followed by the ‘Performers,’ Karnataka (64), Tamil Nadu (59) and Haryana (54).

All remaining States and UTs have  ‘Aspirant’ status. The NITI Aayog noted that the IEMI score is the composite of the three themes, evaluated for each state or UT.

Meanwhile, Kerala has performed well in the adoption of private electric vehicles, where it shares the top ‘Achiever’ slot (100 marks) with Karnataka and Maharashtra. However, in the adoption of EVs in the commercial category and EV-to-EV charger ratio, it is in the ‘Aspirant’ list. In the number of EV start-ups, Kerala has been adjudged a ‘Performer.’

NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba released the report, developed in collaboration with WRI India, on August 4 in New Delhi.

The IEMI score is interpreted as the percentage of e-mobility objectives accomplished by a State or UT. The scores will be updated annually, the NITI Aayog said.

By way of recommendations, the report has urged Kerala to support the push for e-mobility by prioritising low-emission zone policies, scrapping of old vehicles, retrofitting initiatives, and enhanced purchase subsidies. It also advised the State to improve public charging infrastructure by implementing a single-window system and offering concessional land rates for public charging stations. The report noted that Kerala has 1,872 chargers in 1,163 charging stations.

Kerala should establish R&D centres,  centres of excellence, and e-mobility courses for skill development, the report said.

The report also took note of some of Kerala’s significant achievements in e-mobility. The prototype lithium titanate battery developed by the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) and Travancore Titanium Products (TTPL) is “a big step forward for the e-mobility programme,” it said.

Kerala also had the highest electric car penetration rate at 9.1% in March 2025.

# India Electric Mobility Index 2025

  

* 17 Sep 2026
* 7 min read

**Source: HT** 

## Why in News?

The **NITI Aayog** released the 2nd edition of the **India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI)** **2025**, with **Delhi** emerging as the top-performing State/Union Territory in the nation's transition toward electric mobility.  

## What is the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI)?

* **About:** The IEMI is a composite index developed by NITI Aayog in collaboration with World Resources Institute India. It assesses the policy framework, infrastructure readiness, and implementation progress of electric mobility across Indian States and Union Territories.  
  + By providing a transparent benchmarking tool, it aims to foster cooperative and **competitive federalism** in India's transition to clean mobility.
* **Evaluation Framework:** The index evaluates jurisdictions on a **0 to 100 scale, tracking 16 unique performance indicators** categorized into three weighted thematic pillars: 
  + **Transport Electrification Progress (50%):** Measures the **extent of actual EV adoption** across private and commercial segments, along with the effectiveness of governance initiatives, purchase incentives, and operational support.
  + **Charging Infrastructure Readiness (30%):** Evaluates **physical and policy enablers**, including the charger-to-vehicle ratio, power availability, integration of renewable energy, and capital subsidies for charging networks.
  + **EV Research and Innovation Status (20%):** Assesses the **regional innovation ecosystem** by tracking the number of EV start-ups, generated patents, and institutional R&D initiatives.
* **Performance Categories:** Based on their overall scores, States and UTs are classified into four tiers: 
  + **Top Performers:** Scores ≥ 65
  + **Frontrunners:** Scores 50–64
  + **Emerging Performers:** Scores 35–49
  + **Aspirants:** Scores < 35
* **Key Findings of IEMI 2025:** 
  + **Top Performers (Overall):** Delhi retained the highest national score (84, up from 77 in 2024), followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka.
  + **Hilly & North-Eastern States:** **Manipur emerged as the highest-scoring state in this peer group with a score of 46,** followed by Tripura and Assam.
* **Thematic Leaders:** 
  + **Electrification Progress:** Delhi topped this category, closely followed by Chandigarh.
  + **Charging Readiness:** Karnataka led the nation, followed by Maharashtra and Haryana.
  + **Research & Innovation:** Delhi recorded the highest score, alongside strong performances from Maharashtra and Karnataka.
* **Most Improved:** Madhya Pradesh registered the most significant advancement, climbing 16 positions from 23rd in the previous edition to 7th place overall.
* **Surge in EV Adoption:** Electric vehicle sales have grown remarkably, jumping from a mere 0.5% share in 2018 to **8.25% in 2025-26**.  
  + This growth is heavily supported by Central initiatives like the **FAME scheme, PM E-DRIVE, and the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme**.
* **Policy Momentum:** The report highlighted that 29 out of India’s 36 States and UTs have now notified dedicated EV policies, indicating widespread administrative commitment.
* **Strategic Significance**: The index acts as an evidence-based roadmap for subnational governments to transition from initial EV policy formulation to effective implementation.  
  + Scaling up electric mobility is an economic and environmental imperative for India; it is critical for achieving the ***Viksit Bharat 2047*** **vision,** reducing the nation’s 89% dependency on imported crude oil.
* **Environmental and Economic Imperative:** Road transport contributes **12% of India's energy-related** **carbon dioxide emissions**, making the e-mobility transition critical for decarbonisation.  
  + Simultaneously, the automotive sector is economically vital, contributing **7.1% to the national GDP** and employing roughly 19 million people.

## Delhi’s EV Ecosystem

* **Delhi EV Policy 2.0:** Delhi is the first region in India to **mandate 100% electrification of auto-rickshaws** and light commercial vehicles (LCVs) by January 2027, and of two-wheelers by January 2028.
* **Public Transport & Subsidies:** As of early 2026, Delhi operates the largest **electric-bus fleet in India** and remains the first state to provide direct subsidies for electric cycles. 
  + To finance its ambitious Rs 4,000 crore EV subsidy program over the next four years, Delhi is actively seeking Supreme Court permission to utilize unused **Environmental Compensation Charge (ECC) funds.**

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**1. What is the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI)?**  
 The **IEMI, developed by NITI Aayog with WRI India**, benchmarks States and UTs on **EV electrification, charging readiness, and research & innovation**.

**2. Which State/UT topped the IEMI 2025?**  
 **Delhi ranked first with a score of 84**, followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka.

**3. What are the three pillars of IEMI 2025?**  
 The index assesses **Transport Electrification Progress (50%)**, **Charging Infrastructure Readiness (30%)**, and **EV Research & Innovation (20%)**.

**4. What are the major Central schemes supporting EV adoption in India?**  
 Key initiatives include **FAME, PM E-DRIVE and the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme**, supporting EV demand, infrastructure and domestic manufacturing.

**5. What are the key challenges to India’s electric mobility transition?**  
 Major challenges include **charging infrastructure gaps, high upfront costs, battery and critical-mineral dependence, grid readiness, and uneven adoption across States and regions**.

* **Context (PIB):** NITI Aayog launched the **India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI)**, India’s first-of-its-kind tool **to assess subnational EV readiness**.

## About India Electric Mobility Index

* India Electric Mobility Index is a **composite index** measuring the **electric mobility** **ecosystem maturity** across states & UTs.
* **Objective:** It supports **evidence-based policymaking** & promotes **inter-state learning** on EV transition.
* **Dynamic Scoring:** **Scores evolve with changes** in EV policy, adoption, and infrastructure development.

### Methodology

* **Score Range:** Each state or UT is rated **from 0 to 100** using weighted metrics.
* **Indicator Set:** The index uses **16 indicators** grouped under **three key thematic** pillars.
  1. **Electrification:** Measures **EV penetration** across personal, commercial, & public transport segments.
  2. **Charging Readiness:** It evaluates **grid integration**, **station density**, & allied charging infrastructure.
  3. **Innovation:** It captures **manufacturing scale**, **R&D output**, and **EV startup ecosystem activity**.

### State Performance Highlights (2024)

* The index **highlights thematic leadership** across EV adoption, infrastructure, and innovation.
* **Overall Leader:** **Delhi** ranked highest overall, followed by **Maharashtra** and **Chandigarh**.
* **EV Deployment:** **Delhi**, Maharashtra, & Chandigarh emerged as frontrunners in transport electrification.
* **Infra Readiness:** **Haryana**, Karnataka, Ladakh, and Himachal Pradesh led in infrastructure readiness.
* **Innovation Strength:** **Delhi**, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and Karnataka were key innovation frontrunners.
* **Small–State Leader:** **Chandigarh** led among small states and UTs, followed by **Goa** and **Delhi**.

### Significance of India Electric Mobility Index

* IEMI links **mobility outcomes to federal competition** and policy responsiveness.

* **Public Benchmarking:** The index **enables transparent tracking** of EV progress across states and UTs.
* **Federal Competition:** It fosters **cooperative federalism** through competitive rankings & peer learning.
* **Scheme Optimisation:** Findings help recalibrate FAME & PLI **schemes** using subnational outcome data.
* **Data Ecosystem:** It promotes more substantial **EV data collection** and **integration** at the state level.
* **Transparency Lever:** Public rankings **enhance accountability** in electric mobility performance.

# India Launches a Pioneering India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) to Track States/UTs Progress in EV Transition

### 

Posted On:
04 AUG 2025 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog today launched the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI), a first-of-its-kind tool developed to comprehensively track and benchmark the progress of States and Union Territories (UTs) in achieving their Electric Mobility goals.

The Report was released by Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog in presence of Shri B. V. R. Subrahmanyam, CEO, NITI Aayog, Shri. Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, M/o Heavy Industries, Shri O. P. Agarwal, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog and Shri Sudhendu Sinha, Programme Director – E-Mobility, NITI Aayog among other dignitaries.

States are central to India’s ambition of reducing transport sector emissions and achieving net-zero by 2070. Proactive state level action is therefore key to designing tailored policies, deploying supportive infrastructure, and ensuring the benefits of e-mobility reach all communities and geographies equitably.

About the India Electric Mobility Index

The India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) tracks, evaluates and scores all Indian States and UTs out of 100 across 16 indicators under three-core themes: Transport Electrification Progress to capture demand-side adoption, Charging Infrastructure Readiness to track allied charging infrastructure development and EV Research and Innovation Status: Covers supply-side ecosystem R&D efforts.

The IEMI enables evaluation across states and union territories, identifying key drivers of success as well as areas requiring targeted interventions. The Index aims to inform decision-making, foster healthy competition among states, and promote sharing of best practices.

The Index underscores the importance of state-level coordination, integrated planning, and cross-sectoral collaboration in achieving India’s electric mobility vision. By identifying strengths and gaps, the Index aims to support states in aligning with national goals while addressing local needs.

Launching the IEMI dashboard and Report, Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, said that, “The IEMI provides a transparent, comparative framework to assess progress across key themes such as electrification, infrastructure, and innovation. It enables states to benchmark their efforts, identify gaps, and learn from each other’s successes.”

Shri BVR Subrahmanyam, CEO, NITI Aayog, added that, “NITI Aayog has already been at the forefront of enabling the ongoing EV revolution. This index is yet another effort by NITI Aayog to propel India towards its vision of a decarbonized and energy-secure future.”

The IEMI Dashboard can be accessed at: https://iemi.niti.gov.in and the IEMI Report can be accessed at: https://niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-08/India-Electric-Mobility-Index-2024-Report.pdf
